question: Did California's AB 1228 minimum wage for workers at large limited-service restaurant chains ($20 per hour from 1 April 2024; signed 28 September 2023) change employment in California's limited-service restaurants (NAICS 722513) over its first eight quarters, 2024Q2-2026Q1, relative to limited-service restaurants in other states; and did employment already move between the law's signing and its effective date, the one specification choice on which the published QCEW-based studies differ (Clemens, Edwards, Meer and Nguyen, NBER w34033 revised 2026, a decline of about 3.5%; Dube, NBER w35171, 2026, near zero) that no published study varies? The question is contested, not a replication. The new data are modest: the latest published QCEW window ends in 2025Q4 (Clemens et al., w35931), so this adds one preliminary quarter, 2026Q1; the 2026Q2 release is due on 2 December 2026 and the crew does not wait for it.
hypotheses: H1 (first stage, in weekly earnings): the pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT on log average weekly wage (QCEW weekly earnings per job, not the hourly wage the law sets; fewer hours would bias it toward zero) of California NAICS 722513 relative to the comparison group, with the primary estimator fixed at the design gate, is positive: one-sided test at 5%. The inference method must be valid with a single treated state (Ferman-Pinto, conformal, or a permutation whose comparison pool is large enough that a 5% test is attainable without California ranking first by construction); standard errors clustered by state are not used. The design gate shows that the chosen pool and method attain the stated level. Reported also for each year separately, because the $20 fast-food wage did not rise in 2025 or 2026 while California's general minimum did (its premium fell from $4.00 to $3.10). If H1 fails, H2 is reported as uninformative about the wage floor.

H2 (main): the pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT on log employment of California NAICS 722513, same estimator and inference. Decision rule, fixed now, with b = 0.02 log points: compute the two-sided 95% CI [L, U] and the 90% CI [l, u] (a two one-sided test at 5%) with the H1 inference method. Sign: 'negative' if U < 0, 'positive' if L > 0, else 'sign undetermined'. Size: 'smaller than b' if -b < l and u < b, 'at least b' if u < -b or l > b, else 'size undetermined'. The headline label is the pair, in this exhaustive and mutually exclusive table: (negative, at least b) = 'decline of at least 2%'; (negative, smaller than b or size undetermined) = 'decline, size below or not distinguishable from 2%'; (sign undetermined, smaller than b) = 'no effect as large as 2%'; (sign undetermined, size undetermined) = 'inconclusive'; and the positive cases symmetrically. The bound: at the pooled log weekly-wage effect of about 7% that Dube (2026, Table 1 Panel A, SDID, the same pooled post-period estimand) reports, -0.02 is an own-wage elasticity of about -0.29, the size of the more negative published estimates; a CI inside +/-0.02 therefore separates the two published readings. The design stage computes, from pre-2023Q4 data only, the minimum detectable effect at 80% power, and the paper reports it next to H2.

H3 (reduced-form year two minus year one): the ATT on log employment for 2025Q2-2026Q1 minus that for 2024Q2-2025Q1, same estimator and inference, reported next to the yearly H1 wage effects (and the implied yearly own-wage elasticities), because the policy's bite fell in year two and a change cannot be attributed to time alone. 'Larger decline in year two' if the 95% CI of the difference is below 0, 'smaller decline in year two' if above 0, otherwise 'no detectable change'. If the pre-period MDE of the difference exceeds 0.04 (twice b), H3 is reported as uninformative whatever the estimate.

H4 (anticipation; the choice no published study varies): the ATT on log employment averaged over 2023Q4-2024Q1, the two quarters between signing (28 September 2023) and the effective date, relative to a 2023Q3 base, same estimator and inference, with the H2 decision rule and labels. Clemens et al. argue that Dube's 2023Q4 base and 2024Q1 exclusion bias estimates toward zero; w35931 does not vary the base period (footnote 5). A 'negative' finding means a 2023Q4 base absorbs part of the effect, and the paper reports by how much Dube's pooled estimate would move with a 2023Q3 base (descriptive). A 'no effect as large as 2%' finding means the base-period choice cannot explain the disagreement.
contribution: A design fixed and reviewed before any post-2023Q3 outcome is computed: one pre-specified primary estimator, inference valid with a single treated state, an equivalence test against a 2% bound that separates the two published readings, and a direct test of anticipation between signing and the effective date, the choice behind part of the published disagreement that no study varies. The data add one preliminary quarter (2026Q1) to the latest published window (2025Q4); the paper does not claim novelty from data. Existing decompositions of the disagreement (Dube 2026, Tables D1-D2; Clemens et al. w35931, Table A1; Sosinskiy and Reich 2026, Appendix A) are cited, not repeated. The PI and the Scout know the published estimates (disclosed); the analysing roles compute nothing on post-period outcomes before the design gate. Limits known now: QCEW counts jobs and weekly earnings, not hours or hourly wages; part of NAICS 722513 is outside the law's coverage (the published 70% coverage figure refers to 722513 and 722515 together; the share for 722513 alone is not known), so effects on covered jobs are diluted by an unknown factor; some covered chains sit in NAICS 722515, which therefore cannot serve as a control; county cells are suppressed more often from 2025, so the design must say whether the analysis is at state or county level; 2026Q1 is preliminary and will be revised.

tasks.title: Novelty and prior-estimate check: find every study of AB 1228's employment effects (at least Clemens, Edwards and Meer 2025; Dube NBER w35171 2026; Reich and Sosinskiy 2024 or later), record for each the data, period, estimator, comparison group, outcome definition and the headline employment estimate with SE, table and column; say whether any uses QCEW data past 2025Q3; list the specification choices on which Clemens et al. and Dube differ
Fetch QCEW industry slices 722513, 722511, 7225, 10 for 2014Q1 to latest; manifest; prepare county panel; CODEBOOK.md; no CA-vs-other or pre/post statistic
